# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

110	
111	### Core Rules
112	
113	*Every rule below is a data-contract rule of the Item DB module (`src/data/items/` in the code root — location is an ADR candidate), stated so an implementer can write it and a tester can falsify it. Rules are `IDB-n`, numbered and named, as the Graph's LS-n and the kernel's CR-n are. Graph- and registry-sourced numbers are written by their locked name with a `[LSG:n]`/`[REG:n]` tag and appear once; every number this GDD introduces is tagged **[PH]** and is a registry candidate (Section G). Where a rule records an alternative that was considered and rejected, the rejection is part of the rule: a later change must answer it. Examples use only roster `def_id`s (IDB-31) or are marked "illustrative, not in the catalogue", because an example in a GDD is read as a contract.*
114	
115	**IDB-1 — The Item DB is a static, immutable catalogue.** It defines what a thing *is* (mass, ports, ratings, repair part, yield) and what it *fits* (port types, node kind, carry class); nothing on a def says what it is *worth*. It registers **no kernel state block, no step hook, no command and no mutator** — consistent with the kernel's Interactions table (KRN:190-206) having no Item DB row and with CR-6 freezing the block registry at the end of BOOTING [KRN:98]. It is loaded once in BOOTING into an `ItemCatalog`, scene-tree free (kernel H10), read-only afterwards, constructed as `ItemCatalog.new(data, graph_tables)` with both inputs injected and no static, singleton or autoload state (so catalogue tests can build many catalogues in one process; IDB-26) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, and callable from `validate`, from P3 and from presentation, because every query in IDB-28 is pure. It **rejects nothing**: every rejection reason that concerns an item (`BUSY`, `OUT_OF_CHARGES`, `PORT_INCOMPAT`, `NOT_REPAIRABLE`) belongs to Interaction, Suit or the Graph. *Alternative considered:* one WORLD block `items.state` owning every instance with its own id counter — rejected: it duplicates Suit's carried-module state (the index gives Suit "carried modules" [IDX:27]), adds a write path every neighbour must call, and contradicts the producer's advice to keep this system thin and data-shaped [IDX:143]. *Alternative considered:* a hybrid catalogue plus a small `items.loose` block — rejected: it invents ownership the neighbours may not want; the loose-world holder is an Open Question, not a decision made here (IDB-16).
116	
117	**IDB-2 — Six def classes, one prefix and one numeric range each.** Every def belongs to exactly one class, named by its `def_id` prefix and bounded by its `type_id` range; the class fixes the default carry class.
118	
119	| Class | `def_id` prefix | `type_id` range | Default `carry_class` | MVP count | Meaning |
120	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
121	| Module | `mod_` | 1000-1999 | `CARRIED` | 13 | One Graph node (IDB-6); installed, salvaged, patched, repaired |
122	| Tool | `tool_` | 2000-2999 | `HAND` | 3 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: was 4; `tool_suppressant` is dormant, X6)* | A hand-rail tool; never consumed (IDB-11) |
123	| Consumable | `cons_` | 3000-3999 | `STOWED` | 1 | A counted item spent on use (IDB-12) |
124	| Part | `part_` | 4000-4999 | `STOWED` | 5 | Consumed by a full repair (IDB-13) |
125	| Curio | `curio_` | 5000-5999 | `CARRIED` | 1 | Mass with no Graph presence (IDB-14) |
126	| Junk | `junk_` | 9000-9999 | `CARRIED` | 0 (reserved, vertical slice) | A true-mass decoy for phantom salvage (IDB-22) |
127	
128	`CARRIED` means the instance occupies the single `controller.state.carry_ref` [PCI:131, PC-8]; `HAND` means it occupies the hand rail; `STOWED` means it is a counted entry in the Suit's block. The Item DB defines the class; Suit and the Controller own the slots (IDB-16). Capacity is 999 `type_id`s per class (a boot assertion): the class base (1000, 2000, ... 9000) is reserved and never assigned, so the usable range is base+1 to base+999 (orchestrator ruling, QA B8; F-8 and AC-73 pin it). The classes are fixed in the MVP; a seventh class would need a new prefix, a new range and a `catalogue_version` bump (IDB-27).
129	
130	**IDB-3 — Two keys: `def_id` persists, `type_id` stays in memory.** `def_id` is a lowercase ASCII snake_case string `<class>_<family>[_<variant>]`, at most `ID_MAX_LEN` 40 characters [PH], matching `^(mod|tool|cons|part|curio|junk)_[a-z][a-z0-9]*(_[a-z0-9]+)*$` (digits are legal after the first letter: `mod_o2_tank` is a roster id). `type_id` is an unsigned 16-bit integer, append-only, never reused. **Only `def_id` ever reaches a save, a snapshot, a `SalvageRecord`, a hash or a replicated record**; `type_id` exists for in-memory tables and the vertical slice's replication summaries, so renumbering can never break a save. This mirrors the Graph's own contract: "`def_id` is a string and type ids are numbers" [LSG:832], with stable content type IDs under ADR-LSG-08 [LSG:26]. A dialect is a separate field, never an id token (IDB-23). A rename after release is an alias, not a new id (IDB-27). *Alternative considered:* a string key only (no compact in-memory key, nothing to bound a typo) and a numeric key only (contradicts the Graph's string-in-saves rule) — both rejected; the pair is kept in step by the bijection assertion of IDB-4.
131	
132	**IDB-4 — The id ledger and the boot assertions.** A committed ledger `assets/data/items/ids.lock.json` lists every `(def_id, type_id)` pair ever shipped and the `retired_ids[]`. Boot refuses the build with `ITEM_BOOT_TYPE_ID(class, id)`, by analogy to `GRAPH_BOOT_TYPE_ID(table, id)` [LSG:1037], when any of these holds: two defs share a `type_id`; a `type_id` lies outside its class range; a `def_id` prefix disagrees with its class; a `type_id` is in `retired_ids`; a shipped `def_id` appears in the ledger with a different `type_id`; or a ledger pair is missing from the catalogue without a `retired_ids` entry or a `dormant` marker *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Formula F-8 is the assertion. **Dormant entries** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: a ledger pair may carry `dormant: true`, meaning the def is cut from the current build but its interface may return (X6). A dormant pair need not be in the catalogue, no other def may take its `def_id` or its `type_id`, and it may be re-shipped only unchanged (same pair). A dormant pair was never shipped to a save, so it needs no `renamed_from`. At MVP the only dormant entry is `tool_suppressant` 2004; it is distinct from `retired_ids`, which are never reused. Aliases (`renamed_from[]`, IDB-27) are resolved transitively to a depth of at most `ALIAS_DEPTH_MAX` 8 [PH]; a cycle, a self-alias, or an alias equal to a live `def_id` refuses to boot (`ITEM_BOOT_ALIAS(def_id)`), because an alias never creates a def and a retired string reused for a different def would let an old save silently load the wrong thing. The sim never iterates a Dictionary [LSG:64, LS-1 (i)]: the catalogue exposes arrays sorted ascending by `type_id` (`defs_of_class`), and a `def_id`-keyed map is for lookup only.
133	
134	**IDB-5 — Fields every def carries.**
135	
136	| Field | Type | Range / values | Meaning |
137	|---|---|---|---|
138	| `def_id` | string | IDB-3 grammar | Persisted key |
139	| `type_id` | int | IDB-2 range | In-memory key |
140	| `class` | enum | MOD, TOOL, CONS, PART, CURIO, JUNK | Derived from the prefix, asserted equal |
141	| `family` | string | snake_case | Groups dialect variants (IDB-23) |
142	| `dialect` | enum | `foundry` (MVP), `lattice`, `civil` (reserved) | Sprite and port-shape selector only |
143	| `name_key` | string | text key | Localisation key; **no player-facing string lives in a def** |
144	| `sprite_family` | string | art bible 8.5 grammar `<cat>[_<dialect>]_<subject>` | Presentation key; **never a `res://` path**. A module sheet (`mach_<name>`) names its frames by the state tokens `running`, `stopped`, `whole`, `cracked` and, for a lamp, the pair `lit` / `unlit` (In-World Instruments IW-17); the def lists the tokens its sheet draws in `sprite_states` |
145	| `sprite_states` | string[] | subset of `running`, `stopped`, `whole`, `cracked`, `lit`, `unlit`; default empty | Presentation only; read by `has_both_frames` (IDB-28); no sim code reads it |
146	| `cell` | enum | `M96` (96x96, 2x2 tiles), `P48`, `P48x96`, `P96x48`, `T80` (80x80 tool and overlay) | Sprite cell class [ART:1013-1055, 8.2] |
147	| `glyph_id` | string | tools and hand-rail consumables | The hand-rail glyph key: the item's sprite silhouette reduced to the 16 px grid [ART:815]; no bespoke icon |
148	| `mass_g` | int | 1..500000 (g) | True mass of one unit (IDB-21) |
149	| `carry_class` | enum | CARRIED, HAND, STOWED | IDB-2; asserted equal to the class default (a def may not disagree with its class) |
150	| `stack_max` | int | 1..99 | 1 for every CARRIED and HAND def, and for any def with `mass_g` >= `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` |
151	| `salvageable` | bool | default true for modules | Read by Interaction's `begin_cut` `validate`; the Graph does not enforce it [LSG:185] |
152	| `emits` | optional struct `{shape_id, base_pm, hue_class}` | any def that glows: a module (lamp, node lantern) or a consumable (glowstick); absent on every other def | Field *shape* defined in IDB-6; *semantics* are Emitter State's. A def with `emits` and no `lantern_on_states` uses the default of IDB-6 |
153	| `grade` | int | 0 in the MVP | Reserved for Depth Rings & Scarcity; **no behaviour**; never called `tier` (that word is the Graph's power priority); any future use needs a creative-director review (IDB-29 rule 5) |
154	| `renamed_from[]` | string[] | optional | Alias table, honoured only at restore (IDB-27) |
155	| `replaced_by` | string | only on a retired def | Restore remap (IDB-27) |
156	
157	*Forbidden keys (lint).* A def has **no** field named `damage`, `accuracy`, `armour`, `range`, `durability`, `dps`, `xp`, `unlock`, `price`, `value`, `value_gold`, `sell`, `buy`, `cost`, `vendor`, `shop`, `recipe`, `ingredients`, `craft*`, `build_cost`, `editable`, `rarity_weight`, `drop_rate`, `set_bonus`, `win`, `escape`, `quest`, `story_flag`, `lore_text`, `appears_as`, `displayed_as`, `fake_mass`, `lure_sprite` or `hallucination_*`, and no key that makes one item produce another (the single exception is the `repair_part_id` to scrap-yield link of IDB-17). A forbidden key anywhere under `assets/data/items/` refuses to boot (`ITEM_BOOT_FIELD(def_id, field)`). The list is the machine form of guard rails AP-1 to AP-7. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `range` and `durability` added, because AC-22 forbade them while AC-08 did not list them; AC-08 now scans the same list, with the AC-08 extras `speed`, `noise`, `v_carry` and `carry_speed` folded in here as well.)* The extras are forbidden keys too: `speed`, `noise`, `v_carry`, `carry_speed`.
158	
159	**IDB-6 — ModuleDef: the Graph-facing fields, and which are snapshotted.** One def is one Graph node: `install_module(slot_node_id, def_id, hp_start)` installs one `def_id` at one slot node [LSG:184, M5], and no composite def exists. A ModuleDef adds these fields to IDB-5.
160	
161	| Field | Type | Range | Source / status | Graph consumer |
162	|---|---|---|---|---|
163	| `node_kind` | int | an LS-3 node-kind id | read-only mirror of LS-3 [LSG:68] | M5, M6 |
164	| `subtype_id` | int | 0 none; LOAD only: `1 HEATER`, `2 LAMP`, `3 DOOR_MOTOR` | the Graph names `HEATER` but gives it no number [LSG:68]; the Item DB assigns the numbers, append-only; the Graph adopted `1 HEATER`, `2 LAMP`, `3 DOOR_MOTOR` in its Item DB Interactions row *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: confirmed, no longer provisional)* | LOAD `subtype` |

166	| `power_tier` | int | 0..4, or -1 for a node that is not a power consumer | the Graph's `tier` [LSG:68, D.6]: 0 life-critical (scrubber), 1 pumps, 2 doors, 3 lights and the HEATER, 4 other. Renamed `power_tier` in the def so that the word `tier` never means item value; the loader maps `power_tier` to the Graph's `tier` | LOAD `tier` |
167	| `req_w` | int W | 0..5000 | per-def table, IDB-8; D.6 `R_k` range 0-5000 W [LSG:425] | LOAD `req_w` |
168	| `req_max` | int W | `req_w`..5000 | M14 clamps a request to 0..`req_max` [LSG:193]; "the heater's `req_max` is a module-def cap, not a Graph clamp" [LSG:837]. **Read live through `def_id`, never snapshotted** (LS-3 persists LOAD `req_w`, `tier`, `subtype` and `energised_at_step` and no `req_max`); the table of values is IDB-8 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the review proposed snapshotting `req_max` with `req_w`; declined, because LS-3 has no `req_max` field and LSG:837 calls it a module-def cap)* | M14 |
169	| `waste_permille` | int | 0..1000 | per-def table, IDB-8 | D.6, D.7, D.8 heat |
170	| `hp_start` | int bp | 1..10000 (`HP_FULL`); the def default is `HP_FULL` (the Tuning Knobs range 7000-10000 is the advisory guidance for the *default*, IDB-9 is the boot rule) | contract IDB-9 | M5 argument |
171	| `rated_out` | int | per kind | SCRUBBER `R_SCR` (mGU/step); REACTOR `out_w_rated` (W) | D.5; D.6, D.9 |

The lure sprite is the Perception Filter's to draw; the lure-band data and the lie belong to Sanity (SN-21); a def never carries a believed, displayed or fake value. The junk-tell lint (F-10) reads the Sanity-owned band file (registry: `lure_bands.json`; path `assets/data/sanity/lure_bands.json`, SN-21; `{band_id, mid_g, class}`, lint-only, never loaded at runtime or persisted). **No lure data lives under `assets/data/items/`**: the table of what a junk def is dressed as is the lie's data, so neither a junk def nor any file in the Item DB folder says what a thing will look like. Failure & Trail reads the descriptor, not the def (its own Interactions row, FT:305), so the convention is Derelict Authoring's to follow when it authors a dead fault. This is why a thing with `hp` can lack a `def_id`: the Graph gives a `def_id` to every node that is a *module*, and these are structure. The junction node kinds (DUCT_JUNCTION 23, PIPE_JUNCTION 33, FUEL_JUNCTION 41) are not in the MVP slice list [LSG:228] and get no def until a template uses one. **Door motors (resolved).** LS-3 gives a `def_id` to every node except COMPARTMENT, EXTERIOR and HULL_SEGMENT [LSG:68], and the home-ship has door-motor LOAD nodes among its ~8 LOADs [LSG:228] (tier 2 [LSG:425]), so a door motor has a def: `mod_door_motor` (`type_id` 1013; `node_kind` 13, LOAD subtype `3 DOOR_MOTOR`; 120 W, `power_tier` 2, `waste_permille` 0, all [PH] except the tier; IDB-6, IDB-8, IDB-31). The one-sentence reason a thing with `hp` can lack a `def_id` stands: structure (hull segments, edges, openings, seams) is not a module, and the Graph gives a `def_id` only to modules.

395	**IDB-26 — Data lives in JSON under `assets/data/items/`.** One file per class: `modules.json`, `tools.json`, `consumables.json`, `parts.json`, `curios.json` (`junk.json` in the vertical slice), plus `meta.json` (`catalogue_version`, `retired_ids`) and `ids.lock.json` (IDB-4). There is no lure data in this folder (IDB-22). Integers only; any designer float (a 1.5-tile glowstick radius) is converted once at boot by `int(round(x * scale))` into the immutable table, as `GraphTuning` does [LSG:64, LS-1 (b)]; no `res://` path on any field that can reach a save; sprite and glyph keys follow the art bible's 8.5 naming grammar `<cat>[_<dialect>]_<subject>[_<variant tokens>]_<map>.png` [ART:1117-1148]. (i) A def is a typed `RefCounted` class `ItemDef` whose fields are written once by the loader and guarded afterwards; it is not a `Resource` (SL-2 forbids Resource paths, and a `Resource` is editor-mutable shared state) and not a bare Dictionary (`make_read_only` is shallow, so a nested `ports[]` or `verbs[]` would stay mutable; array fields are exposed as read-only copies built once). (ii) An instance is a value type `ItemInstance` (six fields) built only by its constructor or `from_array` and serialised only by `to_array` (IDB-15); there is no Dictionary form. **Immutable** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: GDScript `RefCounted` has reference, not value, semantics, so two holders sharing one object would alias it)*: an `ItemInstance` has no setter after construction; `with_count(n)` and `merged(other)` return **new** objects, and a holder stores the `to_array()` form (never the object) in its persisted state and in `loose[]`, rebuilding an instance with `from_array` when it needs one. `ItemDef` fields are get-only properties written once by the loader. (iii) `ItemCatalog.new(data, graph_tables)` takes both inputs by injection and holds **no static, singleton or autoload state**, so a catalogue test can build many catalogues in one process. (iv) The loader returns an `Array[BootError]` (a plain data class `{code, class_or_table, id, def_id, field, detail}` whose `code` is one value of a code enum) and never calls `assert` (stripped in release builds), `push_error` (which trips gdUnit4) or `quit`; the kernel's BOOTING acts on a non-empty list. (v) Each file is opened by explicit name from the fixed list in this rule (no directory scan), parsed with `JSON.new().parse(text)` so a failure carries `get_error_line()` and `get_error_message()` (`JSON.parse_string` gives no location), and every integer field is range- and integrality-checked at load (`ITEM_BOOT_FIELD`: `40000.5` and `1e9` are refused; an integral float such as `40000.0` is accepted and converted once); **any integer above 2^53 is refused** because a JSON number arrives as `float` and loses precision there. These are MEDIUM-confidence engine claims (no engine-reference module), spike-bound by AC-11. The engine reference has no module for this domain (`modules/` has animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering, ui; there is no `scripting.md` or `core.md`), so these claims are MEDIUM confidence and spike-bound; the 4.7 typed-return rule (an override of a typed-return method needs an explicit `return`) applies to any loader or validator base class.

397	**IDB-27 — Versioning, renames, retirement.** The Item DB offers Save/Load one integer, **`catalogue_version`**, bumped on any def removal, rename or field-shape change (F-9), plus `catalogue_hash` (diagnostic only, never gates a load; H64 over canonical bytes sorted ascending by `def_id` — the function is an ADR candidate). Pre-release saves are disposable [LSG:832]. After the first build given to anyone outside the project, a rename needs a `renamed_from[]` entry on the new def, honoured **only at restore**; a removed def must name `replaced_by` or restore fails loudly with the holder's named failure — `GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` for Graph nodes [LSG:832], the holder's own code for instances; never silently. A value tuned within its type (`mass_g`, `req_w`, a glowstick number) is **not** structural and does not bump. The Item DB does not embed itself in saves. The integer is named `catalogue_version`, the name Save/Load's header table uses [SL:159] and its own Item DB row adopts [SL:476] (name history: Save/Load OQ-13 [SL:1301], closed). This is checkpoint ruling A2 applied to Save/Load's final text: the header is Save/Load's namespace (kernel row 3), so the Item DB carries the owner's written name. `catalogue_hash` is kept as diagnostic. `catalogue_hash` sorts the canonical bytes by `def_id` (ascending byte order), not by `type_id`, so a legal renumber never changes the diagnostic hash.

399	**IDB-28 — The query API (all pure, read-only).** `def(def_id)`, `has(def_id)`, `def_by_type_id(type_id)`, `defs_of_class(class)` (ascending `type_id`, the only order sim code may iterate), `compatible_defs(hardpoint)` (F-6), `repair_part_for(subject_kind, kind_id, loop)` (F-3), `salvage_yield(rec)` (F-5), `weight_class(def)` (F-1), `instance_mass_g(instance)` (F-2), `resolve_alias(def_id)` (restore only), `catalogue_version()`, `catalogue_hash()` and `has_both_frames(def_id, pair) -> bool` (true iff both tokens of `pair` are in the def's `sprite_states`; requested by In-World Instruments IW-17, it implements Sanity AC-SN-152's SPRITE_SWAP eligibility; presentation-only). No query returns a Dictionary iteration order; none mutates; none allocates an instance id. **Pure helpers (orchestrator ruling, QA B2):** `part_cost(subject_kind, kind_id, loop)` (F-4: the count rule only; the channel is Interaction's), `held_mass_g(instances)` (the F-2 holder sum), `validate_instance(instance, graph_step_no)` (IDB-15; returns a reason code, never clamps; `graph_step_no` is the Graph's absolute **10 Hz step** counter, never a 60 Hz tick: the `patched_at_step <= step_no` invariant compares steps with steps, and a harness that passes the kernel tick `T` fails the unit check `graph_step_no = T / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, `fresh_instance(def_id, count, condition_bp) -> ItemInstance or the validate_instance reason code` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, GAP: the owner adds the authoring/seed constructor Derelict Authoring DA-26 needs; it is the single such constructor)*: for a module it forces `count` 1 and requires `condition_bp` in `1..HP_FULL`, with `cap_bp` `HP_FULL`, `patched_at_step` 0 and `charge` 0; for a non-module it requires `condition_bp` 0 and `count` in `1..stack_max`, with `cap_bp`, `patched_at_step` and `charge` 0; it allocates no instance id (CR-8) and never clamps, returning the `validate_instance` reason code for any input that fails, and `glowstick_reach(rem)` (F-7: equals Emitter State's D.9 [EM:506], which reproduces F-7 tick for tick; a **non-authoritative** reference oracle, Emitter State remains authoritative). The analysis formulas (F-1 margin, F-10, F-11, F-12, F-14, F-15) are CI tools in `tools/ci/item_db_lints`, not runtime queries. **Totality (orchestrator ruling, QA B4/B5):** `def` and `def_by_type_id` of an unknown key return the shared immutable sentinel `NO_DEF` (empty `def_id`, `type_id` 0, mass 0; callers test `has` first, and a sentinel reaching a holder is the holder's named failure); `repair_part_for` of an unknown `kind_id` returns (`NONE`, 0); `salvage_yield` of an ABSENT or SALVAGED record returns an empty list; `resolve_alias` outside the restore path returns `NO_DEF`.

428	Five economy rules follow. (1) **A patch is free of items; a part is an upgrade priced in scarcity.** A patch is free of items by locked design [REG:6033], so the part is never the *only* way to survive an MVP fault; it is the only way to stop *paying time* for it. That honest reading of Pillar 5 means **the MVP is always survivable with zero parts for a crew of N = 1: the patch treadmill is a playable, deliberately costly terminal state** (guarantee G-0, an authoring acceptance, **qualified per crew size N** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: "always survivable with zero parts" held only for N = 1 in a 1-to-4-player game; for N >= 2 one scrubber runs a deficit even fully repaired (F-14), so G-0 is "survivable for N = 1; for N >= 2 survivable only until the O2 tank empties unless a second scrubber is installed", and AC-42 is parameterised by N)*; it **holds by LS-10 and M7**: `FAILED` is repairable [LSG:125] and M7 rejects only DESTROYED [LSG:186], so a patch works on the broken breaker at `hp` 2000; the LS-26 phrase "dark until replaced" [LSG:228] is prose, routed to the Graph owner as a wording question, and one spare `mod_breaker_junction` placement is a recommendation to Derelict Authoring, not an Item DB guarantee): the terminal state when the parts are spent is the patch treadmill, and that state is designed as playable. It is a treadmill, not a farm: a patch decays (`PATCH_DECAY_S`), a patched scrubber holds one crew at margin zero, and with N >= 2 crew the treadmill loses ground (F-14: one scrubber, even fully repaired, runs a 200 mGU/step deficit at N = 2; holding N crew takes N patched scrubbers at margin zero and N times the re-patch chores), so zero-part survival is pressure and not a safe place to farm (the Pillar 5 design test). What makes the part worth hunting is quantified in F-14 (a patched scrubber at `PATCH_CAP_BP` makes exactly `R_BREATH` for one crew — margin zero — against a margin of +100 mGU/step for a fully repaired one, and the margin vanishes with a second crew). (2) **Part conservation: no verb converts parts.** `scrap_count` is exactly 1 on every module def in the MVP (boot-asserted), no def consumes a part to yield an item (no recycling, no upgrade), and the number of part instances in existence never exceeds the authored loose parts plus the DESTROYED module nodes. (3) **A supply ratio is an authoring target, not a runtime field.** The ratio of parts supplied to full-repair parts a diligent player could demand, `part_cover_pm` (F-11, now measured per part family and per reachable sortie set, in parts), is held in an advisory band of 500-800 permille [PH]; below it permanent fixes feel out of reach, above it every chronic fault is solved and nothing pushes inward. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: whether a per-family cover of 100 percent is intended is Open Question 38, resolved 2026-10-28 by delegated ruling G2.)* (orchestrator ruling: the three specialist proposals gave 750-1000, 500-750 and 500-800; the reconciled band is 500-800.) (4) **No placement without a consumer**: a module names an install target kind, a part a repair family, a consumable a `use_verb`, a tool its `verbs[]` — a def with no consumer in a placement table is the lint `PLACEMENT_NO_CONSUMER` (WARN; the data core, in the MVP). A lint fails any def or file under `assets/data/items/` that carries a forbidden key (IDB-5). (5) **Depth richness is expressed by placement, never by def stats (BINDING on Derelict Authoring and Depth Rings & Scarcity).** "Deeper Is Richer" is delivered through placement density, part supply (`part_cover_pm` by ring: F-11's band is the MVP default and Depth Rings may set a per-ring target) and authored `hp` (better-condition modules deeper). It is never delivered through def stats: no def carries a worth, dialect is a skin (IDB-23), and `grade` stays 0 and behaviourless; any future behaviour for `grade`, or any stat that differs by ring or dialect, requires a creative-director review before it enters a def.

552	## Formulas
553	
554	All formulas are integer-only: the catalogue is data, and anything an instance carries into a holder block may be hashed or replicated (the kernel's `state_hash` and the Graph's LS-1 (b) rule), so no float is stored, hashed or compared. Truncation is floor, applied to non-negative operands only [LSG:64, LS-1 (d)]. Every duration is labelled **tick** (60 Hz, `TICK_RATE` 60) or **step** (the Graph's 10 Hz, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6) or **s**. Formulas the Graph owns (D.4 `eff`, D.5 `out_scr`, D.14 `seam_at_weld`) are cited by name and line and never restated; where an example needs their value it says "evaluated by calling D.n". The ids F-1 to F-15 are those of IDB-32. Formulas F-1 to F-10 and F-12 are **runtime or boot** formulas; F-11, F-14 and F-15 are **design-time checks** (authoring and balance lints), and F-13 is a derivation that proves a rule by lock.
555	
556	### F-1 `weight_class`
557	
558	The weight_class formula is defined as:
559	
560	`weight_class(m) = LIGHT if m < WEIGHT_MEDIUM_G ; MEDIUM if WEIGHT_MEDIUM_G <= m < WEIGHT_HEAVY_G ; HEAVY if m >= WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` — and the blocking margin lint `margin_ok(m) = for T in {WEIGHT_MEDIUM_G, WEIGHT_HEAVY_G}: abs(m - T) * 1000 >= WEIGHT_CLASS_MARGIN_PM * T`
561	
562	**Variables:**
563	
564	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
565	|---|---|---|---|---|
566	| `m` | int g | 1..500000 | def `mass_g` (IDB-5) | True mass of one unit |
567	| `WEIGHT_MEDIUM_G` | int g | **feasible 4445-5454**, default 5000 (the old range 3000-8000 is infeasible against the roster under the blocking margin) | data [PH] ★ registry candidate | LIGHT/MEDIUM boundary *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
568	| `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` | int g | **feasible 24445-27272** at margin 100, default 25000 (the old range 15000-40000 let the plate silently stop being HEAVY at 40000 and let a full stack of ordinary parts, 15,200 g, reach HEAVY at 15000) | data [PH] ★ registry candidate | MEDIUM/HEAVY boundary *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
569	| `WEIGHT_CLASS_MARGIN_PM` | int permille | **50-150**, default 100 (200 is infeasible: the `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` window closes between 150 and 160) | data [PH] ★ registry candidate | Minimum relative distance of any def's mass from either threshold *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
570	
571	**Output Range:** one of three classes; `margin_ok` is a boolean. Boot assertion `WEIGHT_MEDIUM_G < WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` (`ITEM_BOOT_FIELD`). The margin lint is a blocking CI check (IDB-21), not a boot code. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the lint also computes and prints the feasible window of each threshold from the roster, and a roster-semantic lint asserts the plate is HEAVY and no other STOWED def is; the windows are derived in IDB-21 and are inputs to the registry ranges.)*
572	**Example:** `tool_cutter` 3500 g -> LIGHT (distance to 5000 is 1500 >= 5000 x 100 / 1000 = 500, pass). `curio_data_core` 6000 g -> MEDIUM (1000 >= 500, pass). `mod_battery_cell` 22000 g -> MEDIUM (distance to 25000 is 3000 >= 2500, pass; at the old 25000 g it sat exactly on the threshold, where the `>=` rule made it HEAVY and the lint failed). `mod_coolant_pump` 30000 g -> HEAVY (5000 >= 2500, pass). A def at 24000 g would fail the lint (1000 < 2500) and so cannot ship.
573	
574	### F-2 `instance_mass_g`
575	
576	The instance_mass_g formula is defined as:
577	
578	`instance_mass_g(inst) = mass_g(inst.def_id) * inst.count` ; `held_mass_g(holder) = sum of instance_mass_g over the holder's CARRIED, STOWED and IN_HAND instances` ; `stowed_mass_g(holder) = sum of instance_mass_g over the holder's STOWED instances` (the quantity the binding body cue of IDB-21 reads: `weight_class(stowed_mass_g)` HEAVY means the cue is owed; Suit counts **only the unreserved** count of a stack, because units RESERVED by a FULL job are out of the pack from the begin tick, SE-41, and Suit's `cue_load` also takes the max with the carried class and excludes in-hand tools, SE-28) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
579	
580	**Variables:**
581	
582	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
583	|---|---|---|---|---|
584	| `mass_g(def_id)` | int g | 1..500000 | catalogue | Per-unit true mass |
585	| `inst.count` | int | 1..`stack_max` | `ItemInstance` (IDB-15) | Stack size; 1 for modules, tools and curios |
586	
587	**Output Range:** 0..about 10^7 g (far below 2^53). Mass is **never persisted** on an instance (IDB-15); it is derived from the def on read, so a mass edit needs no migration.
588	**Example:** a player stows 4 `cons_glowstick` (200 g each = 800), 2 `part_pipe_fitting` (1200 g each = 2400) and 1 `part_machine_kit` (2000 g): `held_mass_g` = 800 + 2400 + 2000 = 5200 g; while also carrying a `mod_scrubber` (40000 g, count 1) it is 45200 g. The Suit turns the sum into a body cue (IDB-21); the Item DB supplies only the number. A player who stows one `part_hull_plate` (30000 g) has `stowed_mass_g` 30000, at or above `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` 25000, so the body cue is owed even though no module is carried.

591	
592	The repair_part_for formula is defined as:
593	
594	`repair_part_for(subject_kind, kind_id, loop) = (d.repair_part_id, d.parts_per_full) for NODE with def d ; (node_kind_part[kind_id], 1) for NODE with empty def_id ; (edge_part[(kind_id, loop)], 1) for EDGE ; (NONE, 0) for COMPARTMENT, SEAM, OPENING`

596	**Variables:**
597	
598	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
599	|---|---|---|---|---|
600	| `subject_kind` | enum | NODE 1, EDGE 2, COMPARTMENT 3, SEAM 4, OPENING 5 | Graph M7 [LSG:150, 186] | The function is total over all five values |
601	| `kind_id` | int | an LS-3 node-kind id or an LS-5 edge-kind id | Graph [LSG:68, 72] | Selects the row of IDB-19 |
602	| `loop` | int | 0..5 | Graph [LSG:66] | Needed for PIPE, VALVE and SEAM sub-edges |

607	**Example:** `mod_scrubber` node -> (`part_machine_kit`, 1); `mod_reactor_cell` node -> (`part_machine_kit`, 2); `mod_door_motor` node -> (`part_cable_splice`, 1); the oxygen pinhole DUCT (edge kind 1, loop 1) -> (`part_duct_coupling`, 1); the coolant-leak PIPE (kind 3, loop 3) -> (`part_pipe_fitting`, 1); the fuel-drip PIPE (kind 3, loop 4) -> (`part_pipe_fitting`, 1); a SEAM sub-edge of loop 3 (edge kind 6) -> (`part_pipe_fitting`, 1); HULL_SEGMENT (node kind 50) -> (`part_hull_plate`, 1); a COMPARTMENT, a `SeamRecord` (subject_kind 4) or an OPENING (subject_kind 5) -> (`NONE`, 0).

609	### F-4 `part_cost`
610	
611	The part_cost formula is defined as:
612	
613	`parts_consumed(job) = parts_per_full if the first productive channel step of an accepted FULL job is applied, else 0` ; `stock_after = stock_before - parts_consumed` ; permitted only if `stock_before >= parts_per_full` (Interaction's `validate`) ; `stock_visible = stock_before - parts_per_full` from the Applied FULL begin tick while the record is RESERVED or PAID (released, with no timer, if the channel ends early with no credited block or on an OUTCOME; registry: `full_job_charge`, Interaction's) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* ; `parts_consumed` above is the PAID amount
614	
615	**Variables:**
616	
617	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
618	|---|---|---|---|---|
619	| `parts_per_full` | int | 1..3 | F-3 | Cost of one full job |
620	| `stock_before` | int | 0..`stack_max` x stacks | holder (Suit's block) | Count of the required part def held |
621	| first productive step | event | — | Interaction | The first step in which `hp_cap` or `hp` rises (IDB-20) |
622	
623	**Output Range:** `parts_consumed` is 0 for every PATCH [REG:6033], for a job rejected before its first applied step, and for a FULL on a subject already at `hp_cap` = `HP_FULL` with `hp` = `hp_cap` (`PRECONDITION(NOTHING_TO_REPAIR)`); otherwise `parts_per_full`. A RESERVED part that is never PAID returns to the stock at `until`, so `parts_consumed` 0 can still show a visible dip for one channel. `stock_after >= 0` always.
624	**Example:** a FULL repair of the reactor (`parts_per_full` 2) with 3 `part_machine_kit` held (`stack_max` 2, so stacks of 2 and 1): from the Applied begin tick the visible stock reads 1 (2 kits RESERVED, `full_job_charge`); the first productive step pays them, leaving 1; with no credited block (an early end or an OUTCOME) they are released, with no timer. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* A PATCH on the same reactor spends 0. If the channel is interrupted after the first step the part stays spent and the raised `hp` stays (IDB-20 (3)).

626	### F-5 `salvage_yield`
627	
628	The salvage_yield formula is defined as:
629	
630	`salvage_yield(rec) = [] if rec.state in {ABSENT, SALVAGED} ; [ItemInstance(d.repair_part_id, d.scrap_count, 0, 0, 0, 0)] if rec.state = DESTROYED or rec.hp = 0 ; [ItemInstance(rec.def_id, 1, rec.hp, rec.hp_cap, patched_out, 0)] otherwise (rec.state in {OK, DEGRADED, FAILED} and rec.hp >= 1)` , where `d = def(rec.def_id)` and `patched_out := 0 if rec.hp_cap = HP_FULL else rec.patched_at_step` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, BLOCKING: the branch is keyed on `hp`, not on `state` alone, because the Graph lets a node sit FAILED at `hp` 0 while the warning gate is closed (Graph state-transition table, FAILED to DESTROYED row), and the old state-keyed form would have yielded a module at `condition_bp` 0, which IDB-15 and AC-82 refuse at restore. 633

667	The glowstick_life formula is defined as:
668	
669	`LIFE_TICKS = GLOWSTICK_LIFE_S * TICK_RATE` ; `RADIUS_PX = int(round(GLOWSTICK_RADIUS_TILES * TILE_PX))` ; `WANE_TICKS = floor(LIFE_TICKS * GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM / 1000)` ; `f(rem) = 1000 if rem >= WANE_TICKS else GLOWSTICK_WANE_FLOOR_PM + floor((1000 - GLOWSTICK_WANE_FLOOR_PM) * rem / WANE_TICKS)` ; `reach_px(rem) = floor(RADIUS_PX * f(rem) / 1000)` ; `rem_at_landing = LIFE_TICKS - THROW_ARC_TICKS`
670	
671	**Variables:**
672	
673	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
674	|---|---|---|---|---|
675	| `GLOWSTICK_LIFE_S` | int s | 60-300, default 150 | data [PH] ★ | Seconds of light, counted from the throw tick |
676	| `TICK_RATE` | int | 60 | registry (locked) | Ticks per second |
677	| `GLOWSTICK_RADIUS_TILES` | number | 1.5-3, default 2; strictly below `THROW_RANGE_TILES` 3 [PCI:779] | data [PH] ★ | Radius at full life; converted once at boot |
678	| `TILE_PX` | int | 48 | registry (locked) | Base pixels per tile |
679	| `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM` | int permille | 200-1000, default 400 | data [PH] ★ | Share of total life remaining at which waning starts (1000 = linear from the throw) |
680	| `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FLOOR_PM` | int permille | 100-500, default 250 | data [PH] ★ | Reach fraction at the last tick |
681	| `rem` | int ticks | 0..`LIFE_TICKS` | Emitter State's record (`life_remaining_ticks`) | Life remaining |
682	| `THROW_ARC_TICKS` | int ticks | 30 | Controller [PCI:611] | Flight time; the stick has burned that long before it lands |
683	
684	**Output Range:** `LIFE_TICKS` 3600..18000; `f` in `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FLOOR_PM`..1000, monotone non-increasing as `rem` falls (never rises, never pulses); `reach_px` from `RADIUS_PX` down to the floor reach, then the emitter is removed at `rem` 0. Emitter State owns the evaluation (curve id `WANE_LINEAR_25`, EM-15 [EM:196]); this formula is the parameter contract, and Emitter State's D.9 [EM:506] reproduces it tick for tick (its example: `r` 1800 gives `f` 625 and reach 60; `r` 1 gives reach 24 [EM:520]). Build assertions: `GLOWSTICK_RADIUS_TILES < THROW_RANGE_TILES`; `WANE_TICKS >= 1`. `LIFE_TICKS` is a derivation, not a registry constant.
685	**Example:** `LIFE_TICKS` = 150 x 60 = 9000; `RADIUS_PX` = 2 x 48 = 96; `WANE_TICKS` = floor(9000 x 400 / 1000) = 3600, so the pool is steady for the first 5400 ticks (90 s) after the throw. At `rem` 1800: `f` = 250 + floor(750 x 1800 / 3600) = 625 and `reach_px` = floor(96 x 625 / 1000) = 60 px. At `rem` 3600 the formula is continuous (250 + 750 = 1000). At landing `rem_at_landing` = 9000 - 30 = 8970 (Interaction passes it, EM-15). Floor reach = floor(96 x 250 / 1000) = 24 px, one sixteenth of the full pool's area, which is why Emitter State carries `reach_px` and the shape rather than a radius alone. With `GLOWSTICK_WANE_FROM_PM` 1000 the curve is linear from the throw.
686	
687	### F-8 Id-ledger and bijection assertion
688	
689	The id_ledger formula is defined as:
690	
691	`ledger_ok = (for all d1 != d2: type_id(d1) != type_id(d2) and def_id(d1) != def_id(d2)) and (for all d: floor(type_id(d) / 1000) * 1000 == base(class_of_prefix(d.def_id)) and type_id(d) != base(class_of_prefix(d.def_id))) and (for all d: type_id(d) not in retired_ids) and (for all (id, t) in ids.lock: id in catalogue and catalogue[id].type_id == t, or t in retired_ids, or (id, t) is dormant) and (no def in the catalogue uses the `def_id` or `type_id` of a dormant pair under a different pair) and (count of defs per class <= 999)`
692	
693	**Variables:**
694	
695	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
696	|---|---|---|---|---|
697	| `type_id` | int | 1001..9999 (the six class bases are reserved) | def (IDB-2) | In-memory key |
698	| `base(class)` | int | 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, 9000 | IDB-2 | Class range base |
699	| `retired_ids` | set of int | — | `meta.json` | Ids never to be reused |
700	| `ids.lock` | map def_id -> type_id | — | `ids.lock.json` (IDB-4) | Every pair ever shipped, plus the `dormant` reserved pairs *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
701	
702	**Output Range:** boolean; false raises `ITEM_BOOT_TYPE_ID(class, id)` naming the offending id (a bad alias raises `ITEM_BOOT_ALIAS(def_id)`).
703	**Example:** `mod_scrubber` has prefix `mod`, so its `type_id` must lie in 1000..1999: 1001 passes. Adding a def `mod_gasket` (illustrative, not in the catalogue) with `type_id` 1001 collides with `mod_scrubber` -> `ITEM_BOOT_TYPE_ID(mod, 1001)`. Renumbering `mod_scrubber` to 1020 disagrees with the ledger -> refused. A module given `type_id` 4001 fails the range clause. The next free module id is 1014. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: the ledger holds `tool_suppressant` 2004 as `dormant`; a catalogue that omits it passes, and a catalogue that gives `type_id` 2004 to a different def fails `ITEM_BOOT_TYPE_ID(tool, 2004)`.)*
704	
705	### F-9 `catalogue_version` bump rule
706	
707	The catalogue_version_bump formula is defined as:
708	
709	`catalogue_version' = catalogue_version + 1 if the structural diff between the last released catalogue and this one is non-empty, else catalogue_version` , where structural = {a def removed ; a `def_id` renamed ; a field added to, removed from or retyped in the schema ; a `type_id` range change}
710	
711	**Variables:**
712	
713	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
714	|---|---|---|---|---|
715	| `catalogue_version` | int | 1..2^31 | `meta.json`; offered to Save/Load's header [SL:159] | Starts at 1; monotone |
716	| structural diff | set | — | CI tooling against the last released catalogue | Computed from git |
717	
718	**Output Range:** a monotone non-decreasing integer. **Not structural** (no bump): a value tuned within its type (`mass_g`, `req_w`, a glowstick number, a port `cap`), an edit to a snapshotted-at-install field such as `node_kind` or `ports[]` (a saved node keeps its old value until it is salvaged and reinstalled, IDB-6; a reinstall that no longer fits is caught by the hardpoint lint and `PORT_INCOMPAT`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `repair_part_id` is removed from this list; IDB-6 classes it as **read live** because `repair_part_for` reads the def, so an edit to it changes the repair cost of a node in an existing save at once; it is still not structural (no bump), but the structural-diff tool prints it as a **save-affecting edit**, exactly like a lowered `stock_cap`, so the author knows saved games change the part they ask for)*, and the addition of a new def (an old save cannot name it). `catalogue_hash` is diagnostic and never decides a load. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: a CI note, not a bump: lowering any `stock_cap` is a **save-affecting edit** — the restore rule of IDB-6 moves the excess stock to `discarded_*` and logs it — and the structural diff tool prints it so the author knows a saved game will lose stock.)*
719	**Example:** tuning `mod_scrubber.mass_g` 40000 -> 38000 keeps version 1. Adding `mod_door_motor` keeps the version (an addition). Renaming `part_pipe_fitting` to `part_pipe_clamp` (illustrative, not in the catalogue) bumps to 2 and needs `renamed_from: ["part_pipe_fitting"]`. Removing `tool_scanner` bumps to 2 and needs `replaced_by` or restore fails loudly.
720	
721	### F-10 Junk off-band rule
722	
723	The junk_tell formula is defined as:
724	
725	`tell_pm(junk, lure) = floor(abs(m_junk - m_lure) * 1000 / m_lure)` ; the lint requires `tell_pm >= WEIGHT_TELL_MIN_PM` **and** `weight_class(m_junk) != weight_class(m_lure)` **and** `margin_ok(m_junk)`
726	
727	**Variables:**
728	
729	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
730	|---|---|---|---|---|
731	| `m_junk` | int g | 1..500000 | the junk def's `mass_g` | The decoy's true mass |
732	| `m_lure` | int g | 1..500000 | the lure band's `mid_g`, from the Sanity-owned `lure_bands.json` (registry; SN-21; IDB-22) | The mass the lie dresses it as |
733	| `WEIGHT_TELL_MIN_PM` | int permille | 200-600, default 300 | data [PH] ★ | Minimum relative gap |
734	
735	**Output Range:** `tell_pm` 0..unbounded; pass iff all three clauses hold. The class clause exists because the Suit's cue resolves classes, not grams (IDB-22). Vertical slice only (no junk def ships in the MVP); a junk def that fails is not releasable.
736	**Example:** lure `mod_scrubber` 40000 g (HEAVY). A junk at 21000 g: `tell_pm` = floor(19000 x 1000 / 40000) = 475, class MEDIUM != HEAVY, margin ok (distance to 25000 is 4000 >= 2500) -> pass. A junk at 30000 g: `tell_pm` 250 < 300 and the same class -> fail. A junk at 26000 g: `tell_pm` 350 passes the gap but is HEAVY like the lure -> fail on the class clause (a 14 kg difference gives the same body cue).
737	
738	### F-11 `part_cover` (authoring lint)
739	
740	The part_cover formula is defined as:
741	
742	`demand(f, R) = sum of n over the authored-fault subjects s in the reachable set R that are FULL-repairable with repair_part_for(s) = (f, n)` (**scope** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: an authored fault is a subject Derelict Authoring places already damaged, the eight MVP faults [LSG:228]; an installable module that a player later patches, such as the installable `scr_a`, and the home machines are NOT counted, because their FULL repair is a player-made demand, not an authored one; so `part_machine_kit` has demand 0 by scope and its FULL-repair cost is reported separately in the scope note below), excluding any subject whose part is `NONE` and any subject whose fix is a placed spare module ; `supply(f, R) = loose placements of family f in R + one per authored DESTROYED module node of family f in R` ; `part_cover_pm(f, R) = floor(1000 * supply(f, R) / demand(f, R))`, or `PART_COVER_UNDEFINED` (-1) when `demand(f, R)` is 0 ; the aggregate `part_cover_pm(R) = floor(1000 * sum_f min(supply(f, R), demand(f, R)) / sum_f demand(f, R))` (**each family is capped at its own demand**, so a surplus in one family cannot hide a shortage in another; `PART_COVER_UNDEFINED` when `sum_f demand` is 0) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the uncapped sum let a spare hull plate make duct and pipe shortages read as 500 "in band")* ; advisory band `PART_COVER_MIN_PM <= part_cover_pm <= PART_COVER_MAX_PM`, evaluated per family with `demand(f, R) >= 2` and for the aggregate ; **the per-family band check applies only to a family with `demand(f, R) >= 2`; a family with demand 1 can only read 0 (`PART_TYPE_UNSUPPLIED`) or >= 1000 and is printed, not band-checked; the aggregate is always band-checked** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix), GAP: the owner adds the exemption, because without it every authored family with a single fault would warn `PART_COVER_BAND` forever and the shipped ledger could never be clean)* ; warning `PART_TYPE_UNSUPPLIED(f, R)` when `demand(f, R) > 0` and `supply(f, R) = 0` (registry: `part_cover_pm`, requested 2026-10-27, expression revised by the design review; this GDD is its source, Derelict Authoring reads it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier type-blind form divided parts by repairs, so a 714 permille "in band" hid a machine-kit cover of 0, the reactor's 2-part cost, and subjects that cannot take a part at all)*
743	
744	**Variables:**
745	
746	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
747	|---|---|---|---|---|
748	| `f` | family | `part_duct_coupling`, `part_cable_splice`, `part_pipe_fitting`, `part_hull_plate`, `part_machine_kit` | IDB-13 | A part family |
749	| `R` | set of sections | the cumulative loaded set after sortie k (Derelict Authoring's access order, D.4; Boarding's loaded sets S0 to S4) | Authoring | The reachable sortie set |
750	| `supply(f, R)` | int parts | 0.. | Derelict Authoring's placements plus one per DESTROYED module node (`scrap_count` pinned to 1); `supply_max(f, R)` is also printed: modules in R of family f that a player could destroy on purpose (not added to `supply`) | Finite parts of family f in R |
751	| `demand(f, R)` | int parts | 0.. | counted from the FULL-repairable subjects in R, **in parts** (the reactor counts 2), excluding subjects with `repair_part_for` `NONE` (the O2 seam record) and subjects whose fix is a placed spare module (the broken junction, covered in kind by the spare breaker) | Parts a diligent player could spend on family f |
752	| `PART_COVER_MIN_PM` | int permille | 400-600, default 500 | data [PH] | Below it permanent fixes feel out of reach |
753	| `PART_COVER_MAX_PM` | int permille | 700-900, default 800 | data [PH] | Above it every chronic fault is solved and nothing pushes inward |
754	
755	**Output Range:** permille, 0..unbounded, or `PART_COVER_UNDEFINED` (reported, never divided); the per-family band check applies only to a family with `demand(f, R) >= 2` (a demand-1 family reads 0 or >= 1000 and is printed, not band-checked) and the aggregate is always band-checked *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the band is advisory (a warning, not a CI failure), as is `PART_TYPE_UNSUPPLIED` (its id is proposed to Derelict Authoring's `content_lint_ids`, which owns lint ids). A design-time check, never a runtime field. An early reachable set (after sortie 1) is expected to warn: Derelict Authoring deliberately places the pipe and duct parts on the second sortie (DA-25), so the lint reports that as a logged "uncovered by choice" entry, not a defect.
756	**Example (MVP numbers, Derelict Authoring's ledger DA-25; Authoring owns the real counts):** of the eight MVP faults [LSG:228], the pump stall is STARVE and takes no part, the reactor SCRAM is cleared by a reset, the O2 seam is a `SeamRecord` (`repair_part_for` `NONE`) and the broken junction is covered in kind by the spare `mod_breaker_junction`; that leaves five FULL-repairable, part-taking subjects at one part each: the pinhole DUCT (`part_duct_coupling`), the overloaded CABLE (`part_cable_splice`), the coolant PIPE and the fuel PIPE (`part_pipe_fitting` x 2) and the fatigued HULL_SEGMENT (`part_hull_plate`): demand 5 parts. Supply (all sections reachable; 4 loose parts, Derelict Authoring's tightened ledger DA-25, delegated ruling G2) is duct 1, cable 1, pipe 1, hull 1, kit 0 = 4 against demand 5 (duct 1, cable 1, pipe 2, hull 1). Per family: duct 1000, cable 1000 and hull 1000 (demand 1, printed, not band-checked), pipe floor(1000 x 1 / 2) = 500 (in band, at its lower edge); `part_machine_kit` demand 0 and supply 0 -> `PART_COVER_UNDEFINED`, no warning; aggregate floor(1000 x (1 + 1 + 1 + 1) / 5) = **800, inside the band at its top edge** (the cap changes nothing here: no family has surplus). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* **Scope note:** the demand above is the authored faults only. The installable `scr_a` (DA-47 supplies its home slot) and the home machines are not counted; a FULL repair of a patched scrubber needs `part_machine_kit`, which the MVP never places, so the permanent fix of a scrubber is unreachable in the MVP by content and `part_machine_kit` reads `PART_COVER_UNDEFINED` (0 of 0) by scope rather than `PART_TYPE_UNSUPPLIED`; whether that is intended scarcity or a content gap is Open Question 48, and F-14 is computed at the patch cap for that reason. The real MVP cover is complete in every family except pipe, where one fitting serves two pipe faults; the old type-blind figure of 714 (demand 7 counting the seam and the junction, parts divided by repairs) hid; whether 100 percent family cover is intended (Open Question 38) is resolved 2026-10-28 by delegated ruling G2: Derelict Authoring removed one `part_pipe_fitting` and the ledger now reads 800. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **`supply_max` by family, printed beside `supply`:** it counts the modules of each family a player could destroy on purpose. `part_machine_kit`: the ten machine defs placed in R (scrubbers, the reactor, batteries, pumps, radiators, reservoirs, tanks, vents, heaters); `part_cable_splice`: every `mod_lamp`, `mod_door_motor` and `mod_breaker_junction` placed in R, which is the large family (Derelict Authoring counts 26 LOAD nodes world-wide, lamps, the beacon, door motors and heaters, and the heaters scrap to machine kits, so the cable-splice `supply_max` is on the order of twenty before breaker junctions are added; the lint prints the exact figure) against an authored cable demand of 1 and an authored cable supply of 1. So the single placed splice is not the only splice in the world: a player who destroys a lamp on purpose holds a second. Whether lamps should scrap to a part at all is Open Question 39 (creative direction, not decided here); until it is, the anchor beat's "earned" reading holds for the *placed* splice only. After sortie 1 only (home plus derelict A): demand is duct 1, cable 1, pipe 2 (the home faults) = 4; supply is cable 1 and hull 1 (the plate has no demand until derelict B is welded); `PART_TYPE_UNSUPPLIED` fires for duct and pipe, the intended scarcity of DA-25 ("the first fault cannot be fully repaired until the second sortie"). **Capped aggregate: floor(1000 x (min(1,1) + min(1,0)) / 4) = 250, below the band**, where the old uncapped sum read floor(1000 x 2 / 4) = 500 "in band" because the unusable plate stood in for the missing duct and pipe parts *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Per-set capped aggregates of the MVP ledger *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: S0 0, S1 250 (as above), S2 and S3 400, S4 800. Generic capped aggregates (no surplus in any family; demand 5 in one family): supply 3 of 5 -> 600, in band; 4 of 5 -> 800, in band (the edge); 2 of 5 -> 400, below 500. (orchestrator ruling: IDB-29 reconciled the specialists' bands of 750-1000, 500-750 and 500-800 to 500-800.) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review.)*

778	### F-13 Haul cost (mass-independent by lock)
779	
780	The haul_cost formula is defined as:
781	
782	`ticks_carry = D_tiles * TILE_PX / V_CARRY` ; `noise_carry = ticks_carry * NOISE_PER_TICK_carry` ; `ticks_empty = D_tiles * TILE_PX / V_RUN` ; `noise_empty = ticks_empty * NOISE_PER_TICK_run` ; and, *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, with `heavy_stowed` true when the holder has any STOWED instance of `weight_class` HEAVY (IDB-13, D18): `ticks_empty_hs = D_tiles * TILE_PX / V_WALK` ; `noise_empty_hs = ticks_empty_hs * NOISE_PER_TICK_walk` ; `ticks_carry` and `noise_carry` are unchanged by `heavy_stowed` (the carry gait is already `V_CARRY`).
783	
784	**Variables:**
785	
786	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
787	|---|---|---|---|---|
788	| `D_tiles` | int | 1..about 60 | map | One-way distance in tiles |
789	| `TILE_PX` | int | 48 | registry (locked) | Base pixels per tile |
790	| `V_CARRY` | int px/tick | 1 | registry [REG:5338-5356] (locked) | Flat carry speed; **not** scaled by mass |
791	| `V_RUN` | int px/tick | 3 | registry [REG:5317-5337] (owner: Player Controller & Input, [PCI:238]); locked | Empty run speed |
792	| `V_WALK` | int px/tick | 2 | registry (owner: Player Controller & Input); locked | Walk speed, the empty-handed gait while a HEAVY item is stowed *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
793	| `NOISE_PER_TICK` | int | walk 1, carry 1, run 4 | registry [REG:5442-5457] (locked) | Attention units per tick *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |

795	**Output Range:** ticks 48..2880 for D 1..60 carrying; mass appears nowhere in the expression, which is the point: the Item DB cannot make a heavy thing slower or louder without a registry conflict. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: this expression covers the single carried module; Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: a stowed HEAVY item (the 30 kg plate) no longer costs nothing. Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): option (a) of D18, Open Question 32: while any HEAVY item is stowed, `run` is disabled, with no grams-based term and `V_CARRY` and `NOISE_PER_TICK` locked. The plate is therefore a priced second load, not a free second slot. AC-46 asserts the values derived below.)*
796	
797	**Derivation of the plate's price (constraint and arithmetic).** *Constraint:* the stowed plate must cost something a regression test can detect, without a mass term and without touching `V_CARRY` or `NOISE_PER_TICK`. The only free variable the ruling leaves is the empty-handed gait. With the plate stowed the empty gait drops from `V_RUN` 3 to `V_WALK` 2 px/tick, so the added time per tile is 48/2 - 48/3 = 24 - 16 = 8 ticks, a factor of 1.5. *Noise:* walking is quieter than running (1 against 4 per tick, so 24 against 64 per tile), so the plate does not add noise; it lengthens the exposure on the clock (the cost the player feels is time and, through Attention's time-based terms, the exposure that time carries), and Attention's X3 carry intake (keyed on HEAVY) is the route by which the burden becomes a legible stimulus, not this GDD. *While a module is carried* the gait is already `V_CARRY` 1, so the plate adds nothing: the price falls only on the empty-handed legs, which is the leg on which the free slot was free.
798	
799	**Example (plate stowed, 30 tiles, empty hands):** `ticks_empty_hs` = 30 x 48 / 2 = 720 ticks (12 s) and `noise_empty_hs` = 720 x 1 = 720; the same 30 tiles without the plate: `ticks_empty` = 480 ticks (8 s) and `noise_empty` = 1920. The plate costs +240 ticks (+50 percent) on a 30-tile empty leg and 1200 fewer noise units. With a carried `mod_reactor_cell` and the plate stowed: 1440 ticks and 1440 noise, identical to the carry without the plate. Passes the constraint: a regression that re-enables run changes 720 to 480. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Exact values with the run ramp:** the Controller's `RUN_RAMP_TICKS` 6 starts every run at `V_WALK` for 6 ticks (12 px), so the unplated 30-tile run is 6 + (1440 - 12) / 3 = **482 ticks** and 6 x 1 + 476 x 4 = **1910 noise units**; the figures 480 and 1920 above are the idealised no-ramp values, and the plate's exact cost on that leg is 720 - 482 = +238 ticks.
800	
801	**Pursuit exposure: what the plate actually costs** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Walking is always available, so the noise column understates the plate. The price is the **escape gait**: with a plate stowed the holder cannot reach `V_RUN`, so a pursuer whose speed `v_p` (px/tick, Horror Entities' number, not valued here) satisfies `V_WALK` <= `v_p` < `V_RUN` can be outrun by an unplated holder and cannot be outrun by a plated one; over a leg of `D` tiles a plated holder is exposed for `8 x D` extra ticks (48/2 - 48/3 per tile, ramp aside) and a pursuer covers `v_p x 8 x D` px more ground in that time. Over the 30-tile reference leg that is 240 extra ticks of exposure. The plate is therefore **slow to flee**, not loud: the MDA claim is reworded accordingly. **Attention C33 answered (this GDD's half)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*: Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling R5 (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): a stowed HEAVY item adds **no** `BURDEN` push. The burden is keyed on `carry_ref` (X3) and on salvage carry only (delegated ruling R5), a stowed plate is not a `carry_ref` carry, and charging it twice (burden for the gait it already lost) would double-price one cost; Attention keeps C33 closed on that reading and its refresh is owed no further change by the Item DB. **Single implementation:** the HEAVY-stowed test is Suit's `stowed_heavy(player_id)` (SE-41, which excludes units RESERVED by a FULL job and is derived on read), not a per-def check: the rule reads "any **unreserved** STOWED instance of `weight_class` HEAVY". A reserved plate (a FULL job holds it) therefore produces no run toggle, and no visible switch occurs when the reservation begins or is released early *(CD agreed with the gameplay-programmer: the earlier alternative rules would duplicate Suit)*. The Item DB's contribution is the class (`weight_class` HEAVY, F-1), Suit's is the sum and the reservation. **Reconciliation** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: D18's user wording is "any HEAVY item is stowed", Suit's `stowed_heavy` is sum-based (its stowed weight class is HEAVY), and IDB-13 was per-def. Under G1 the publisher's reading is canonical, so Suit's `stowed_heavy` is the implementation. In the MVP the readings coincide: the plate is the only HEAVY def, and the largest ordinary stack without it is 15,200 g, below `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` (AC-46 (iv)). The divergence case (a post-MVP stowed sum at or above `WEIGHT_HEAVY_G` with no plate) is folded into Open Question 35 (Suit's class margin and hysteresis).
802	**Example:** a 30-tile trip carrying `mod_reactor_cell` (90000 g): `ticks_carry` = 30 x 48 / 1 = 1440 ticks (24 s) and `noise_carry` 1440; the same trip carrying `curio_data_core` (6000 g) is identical. The empty run out is 1440 / 3 = 480 ticks (8 s) and 1920 noise units; the round trip is 1920 ticks (32 s) and 3360 noise. Walking the same 30 tiles takes 720 ticks, so carrying costs twice the time and, per tile, twice the noise (48 vs 24).

804	### F-14 Scrubber margin ladder (why a part is worth a sortie)
805	
806	The scrubber_margin formula is defined as:
807	
808	`margin(hp, N) = out_scr(hp) - N * R_BREATH` where `out_scr(hp)` is the Graph's D.5 evaluated at `sat` 1000 with `eff` from D.4 (cited, not restated) ; `scrubbers_to_hold(N, hp) = ceil(N * R_BREATH / out_scr(hp))` (the least count with margin >= 0) ; `scrubbers_with_margin(N, hp) = floor(N * R_BREATH / out_scr(hp)) + 1` (the least count with margin > 0, **strict-margin semantics, the design's standard**, because a margin of exactly zero "loses the room" at any wear: the Graph's own tuning note [LSG:927]) ; both return the sentinel `SCRUBBERS_UNDEFINED` = -1 when `out_scr(hp)` is 0, i.e. at or below `HP_FAIL` (no finite count exists) ; `T_hold = PATCH_DECAY_S` (240 s) is the maintenance interval of a life-critical scrubber at the patch ceiling: past it the patch decays and the margin goes negative, and duty wear (LSG:226) can shorten it ; `chore_per_hour_max = floor(3600 / T_hold)` re-patches, an **upper bound** (the earlier name `chore_per_hour` is retired), because it ignores the O2 tank buffer and the re-patch delay: the real interval is `T_hold` plus the time the tank takes to absorb the post-hold deficit, plus the player's reaction delay *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* ; `tank_steps(N, S, hp) = floor(stock / (N * R_BREATH - S * out_scr(hp)))` when the deficit `N * R_BREATH - S * out_scr(hp)` is positive, else `TANK_NEVER` (-1), with `stock` the O2 tank's stock (3,000,000 mGU at the shipped value) and 10 steps to the second (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` 6 at `TICK_RATE` 60), which is the tank-drawdown model that replaces the 15-per-hour figure as the planning number *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `scrubbers_needed` was off by one at exact divisibility — N = 4 at `hp` 10000 needs 3 scrubbers to reach margin 0 but 4 for a positive margin — and its UNDEFINED sentinel was not defined; the earlier `T_decay_cycle` 540 s as the maintenance interval was the time to FAILED, not the time to a negative margin, and understated the chore load by about 2.25x)*

For two crew with one scrubber at `hp` 10000 the deficit is 600 - 400 = 200 mGU/step and the home-ship's 3,000,000 mGU O2 tank lasts 3,000,000 / 200 = 15,000 steps = 25 min; for four crew the deficit is 800 and the tank lasts 3750 steps = 6.25 min. **Those two figures need a `HP_FULL` scrubber, which the MVP cannot reach (no `part_machine_kit` is placed, F-11 scope note).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **At the reachable ceiling, `PATCH_CAP_BP` 6000 (`out` 300):** N = 2 with one scrubber has a deficit of 600 - 300 = 300 mGU/step and the tank lasts 10,000 steps = 1,000 s = **16.7 min** (not 25); N = 4 has a deficit of 1200 - 300 = 900 and the tank lasts 3,333 steps = **5.6 min** (not 6.25); `scrubbers_to_hold(N, 6000)` = N and `scrubbers_with_margin(N, 6000)` = N + 1. 824	
825	> **WITHDRAWN as a blocking item — retained as a historical note** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. F-15, AC-94 and `T_CYCLE_MIN` are no longer blocking and no longer gate anything. The review found the formula compared the cost of one salvage cycle against the whole patch chore over a horizon, which are not comparable; that its `T_decay_cycle` of 540 s understated the chore load (the life-critical interval is `T_hold` 240 s, see F-14); and that its tripwire is redundant now that IDB-18 closes the launder by rule and the split persistence tests AC-32a to AC-32f are the real control. The heading stays so the formula register (IDB-32) keeps its ids; the body below is kept for the record and is not a requirement.

827	The patch_launder formula is defined as:
828	
829	`launder_pays_off <=> T_cycle < floor(H / T_decay_cycle) * (c_patch + w_patch)`

831	**Variables:**
832	
833	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
834	|---|---|---|---|---|
835	| `T_cycle` | s | Interaction's and Assembly's | cut + carry + `cap_port` on the stubs + install | Time cost of one salvage-then-reinstall of a patched module |

837	| `T_decay_cycle` | s | 540 for a machine (to FAILED), 440 for a leak subject | Graph [LSG:769]: 240 s hold (`PATCH_DECAY_S`) plus 30 or 20 wear periods of 10 s at `PATCH_DECAY_BP_PER_100` 100 | Interval between mandatory re-patches |

Under the adopted rule (IDB-18: a reinstall carries `hp_cap` and `patched_at_step`) the launder does not exist, so this check is **no longer the control**; it is a regression tripwire and the Graph owner's fallback arithmetic. It answers one question: if a build or a ruling ever lets a reinstall reset the cap or the clock (`hp_cap` `HP_FULL`, no `patched_at_step`), would cycling pay? The primary control is the persistence rule and its test (AC-32: cap and clock must come back unchanged); this check is the second line. In no case does a cycle launder the damage (`hp` is unchanged) or duty wear.
841	**Example:** (all times illustrative until Interaction is written) *had the rule been the other way*: for a patched scrubber over `H` 3600 s, `T_decay_cycle` 540 gives floor(3600 / 540) = 6 re-patches x (8 + 15) = 138 s of chore, and a salvage-reinstall in one room at a 35 s illustrative `T_cycle` would be cheaper, so the launder would pay off at the placeholders, at the price of the cut's stub hiss (F-12: the scrubber's one O2 stub, port 101 per IDB-7, leaks 200 mGU/step until capped), the island re-solving without the scrubber and an Attention spike.
